name: meeple-loop-no-starting-meeples-v1
description: ⚠️ 09/09/2026, THE COMMONS FLIP: THIS ARM NOW PINS THE PASSENGERS AS WELL. Dean ruled the commons in as the engine DEFAULT (docs/commons-handoff-2026-09-09-v1.md), which moved four leaves at once - rules.turn.visitCurrency to 'commons', rules.turn.bonusTiming to 'start', rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour to 0, and the Orchard door's printed draw to 2/2. An overlay that pins only what it is named for stops being the arm it is called, silently, which is the 05/09/2026 lesson written down: NAME THE PASSENGERS BEFORE RULING AN ARM IN. So the `set` below carries every leaf this arm's game relied on, whether or not it was in the original experiment. ⭐ AND NOTE WHAT THE FLIP DID TO THIS PARTICULAR ARM: rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour 0 is now the SHIPPED value, so the leaf this arm exists to set no longer looks like a change at all. It is kept explicit for exactly that reason - read beside the visitCurrency pin it is still the meeple loop with no ignition, which measured a hook of 0.09 and an empty-board Collect on 87% of turns. ⭐ 05/09/2026: DEAN RULED R17 IN AND THE ENGINE DEFAULTS MOVED WITH IT. The shipped game is now meepleAsCard true, meepleAsCardGoesTo 'board', slotToll 1 and meepleCapPerColour 2, which is exactly overlays/meeple-on-board-v1.overlay.json. ⚠️ SO THIS OVERLAY NOW PINS THE v1 LOOP EXPLICITLY (meepleAsCard false, slotToll null, meepleCapPerColour 1) on top of its own knob, because it is the ignition control of the v1 LOOP and the default is no longer that loop. Its own sweep value still wins over the pin. The equivalent sweep under the SHIPPED rules is overlays/meeple-on-board-cap-one-v1.overlay.json and -cap-three- for the cap; the others have no R17 twin yet. THE BOOTSTRAP CONTROL for the meeple loop. The design hands every player one meeple of EACH of the five colours at setup, not drawn from the island bag, so a seat can visit any open door from turn one. This arm starts every supply EMPTY and asks what that gift is actually paying for. IT IS A REAL QUESTION AND NOT A TIDY-UP, because the starting five are the entire reason the loop can turn at all in the opening: with no meeples in supply the only legal bonus is Collect on an empty board, which is a bare Draw 1, and the first meeple anyone can spend has to arrive from an island delivery - which needs a barn, which needs a harvest, which needs several turns of building. THE PREDICTION. An empty start should push the whole visit economy several rounds later, flatten the hook badly in the first third, and make the opening indistinguishable from the v31 game it is meant to replace. If it does NOT - if the hook recovers to near the shipped arm's figure - then the starting five are pure acceleration rather than the engine's ignition, and the component count question in the handoff (5 per player plus 1 per tile is 32 at four seats against a bag of 25) gets much easier, because the bag stops needing to grow. READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) the hook by game third, not just the whole-game figure, because this arm's whole effect is a delay and a single average will hide it; (2) the bonus mix, watching the empty-board collect share in the first third, which is the solitaire opening this arm risks creating; (3) game length, because a loop that starts late is a longer game; (4) deliveries per player, since island meeples are now the ONLY source and the delivery rate and the visit rate become the same curve. TREAT A GOOD RESULT HERE WITH SUSPICION: the bots are self-regarding and price a meeple given to a rival at zero, so they will underweight exactly the circulation this arm removes. ⚠️ STATUS, 04/09/2026: the meeple loop is now the shipped default, so the visitCurrency line in this overlay's `set` is redundant and is kept only to say what the arm is a variant of. startingMeeplesPerColour 0 is still a live variant, and the answer it gave is now part of the shipped design's justification rather than an open question: the hook collapsed to 0.09 and the empty-board collect took 87% of turns, so the starting five are the loop's ignition and the bag has to grow to carry them. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
